themes.label: Mind & Words
themes.blurb: Where you talk yourself out of feeling, or talk over what's true.

prompts.prompt: What truth about myself do I avoid saying out loud, even to people I trust?
prompts.followUp: If I said it anyway, right now, what's the worst thing I imagine would happen — and how likely is that, really?

prompts.prompt: Which emotions do I find hardest to put into words?
prompts.followUp: When I can't name what I'm feeling, what do I do instead — go quiet, get sarcastic, change the subject, overexplain?

prompts.prompt: How do I use overthinking to avoid actually feeling something?
prompts.followUp: What would happen if, just once, I let the feeling move through me before I tried to analyze it?

themes.label: Worth & Love
themes.blurb: Where love, money, and self-worth get tangled into one fear.

prompts.prompt: What fears stop me from fully letting someone love me?
prompts.followUp: Whose love, growing up, came with conditions — and am I still meeting those same conditions for people now?

prompts.prompt: How do I seek validation from others, and what would it take to give that to myself instead?
prompts.followUp: What's one thing I did well this week that I haven't told anyone, because I was waiting for someone else to notice first?

prompts.prompt: How do I handle rejection, and what does my reaction say about how I see my own worth?
prompts.followUp: If a friend described being rejected the way I just described it, would I tell them it meant the same thing about their worth?

themes.label: Anger & Drive
themes.blurb: Where action turns into self-sabotage, or anger turns inward.

prompts.prompt: How do I sabotage my own success, and why might I be doing this?
prompts.followUp: What would I have to risk losing if I actually let myself succeed without sabotaging it?

prompts.prompt: What tends to trigger my temper fastest, and what is usually underneath the anger?
prompts.followUp: The last time I snapped at someone, what was I actually afraid of in that moment?

prompts.prompt: How do I tend to avoid discomfort, and what might happen if I moved straight through it instead of around it?
prompts.followUp: What's one uncomfortable conversation or task I've been circling for weeks — and what's the smallest first step toward it?

themes.label: Belief & Expansion
themes.blurb: Where limiting beliefs and overpromising both come from the same fear of not enough.

prompts.prompt: What limiting beliefs are holding me back from the life I actually want?
prompts.followUp: Where did I first learn to believe that — and whose voice does it sound like?

prompts.prompt: Where in my life do I overpromise or overcommit, and what am I trying to prove when I do?
prompts.followUp: What would it feel like to disappoint someone by simply telling them the truth up front?

prompts.prompt: When I think about my future, what fears come up most frequently?
prompts.followUp: If that fear came true tomorrow, what is the very first thing I would actually do?

themes.label: Inner Critic & Limits
themes.blurb: Where the inner critic enforces rules that were never really yours to keep.

prompts.prompt: What does my inner critic say to me most often, and whose voice does it actually sound like?
prompts.followUp: If I spoke to myself the way I speak to someone I love, what would today's inner monologue sound like instead?

prompts.prompt: What boundaries do I struggle to maintain, and what am I afraid will happen if I hold them?
prompts.followUp: Who in my life reacts the worst when I do hold a boundary — and what does their reaction usually talk me into doing?

prompts.prompt: How do I react when someone criticizes me, and what does that reaction protect?
prompts.followUp: What's the difference between criticism that's actually useful and criticism that just confirms what I already feared about myself?

themes.label: Detachment & Independence
themes.blurb: Where independence turns into a wall instead of a strength.

prompts.prompt: Which of my personality traits do I try to hide from others, and what would happen if I didn't?
prompts.followUp: Who has earned the right to see the version of me I usually keep hidden — and have I let them?

prompts.prompt: Do I use independence to avoid needing people, and if so, what am I protecting myself from?
prompts.followUp: What's one small thing I could ask for help with this week, just to practice being needed without it costing me anything?

prompts.prompt: When do I retreat into logic or distance instead of staying present with how I actually feel?
prompts.followUp: What feeling was I avoiding the last time I told myself 'it's fine, it doesn't matter'?

themes.label: Illusion & Letting Go
themes.blurb: Where denial, escapism, and old grudges all serve the same purpose: avoiding what's real.

prompts.prompt: What aspects of myself am I in denial about, and how can I start to confront them honestly?
prompts.followUp: If a close friend named this thing about me out loud, would I feel exposed, relieved, or both — and why?

prompts.prompt: What grudges am I still holding onto, and how are they actually serving me?
prompts.followUp: What would I lose, besides the grudge itself, if I let this one go today?

prompts.prompt: How do I escape from feelings I don't want to deal with — distraction, fantasy, substances, scrolling?
prompts.followUp: What is usually waiting underneath, in the ten minutes right before I reach for the escape?

themes.label: Power & the Unconscious
themes.blurb: Where control, secrecy, and shame guard the parts of you that feel most dangerous to show.

prompts.prompt: What part of myself am I most ashamed of, and how can I learn to accept it?
prompts.followUp: If that part of me were a person, what would it need to hear to finally feel safe?

prompts.prompt: In which areas of my life do I feel powerless, and what would it look like to reclaim even a small piece of that power?
prompts.followUp: Who or what currently holds the power I wish I had in that area — and how did they end up holding it?

prompts.prompt: How does my shadow self show up when I'm under stress — controlling, secretive, jealous, withdrawn?
prompts.followUp: What was the very first situation, even far back in childhood, where that reaction kept me safe?

themes.label: Feeling & Roots
themes.blurb: Where childhood patterns still decide how safe vulnerability feels today.

prompts.prompt: What childhood wounds am I still carrying, and how do they show up in my closest relationships today?
prompts.followUp: What did I need to hear back then that nobody said — and could I say it to myself now?

prompts.prompt: When was the last time I felt truly vulnerable, and what did that moment teach me?
prompts.followUp: Did I let anyone see that vulnerability, or did I process it entirely alone — and why?

prompts.prompt: Where do I over-give or over-protect the people I love, and what am I afraid would happen if I stopped?
prompts.followUp: What does it cost me, physically and emotionally, to keep giving past the point I actually have left to give?

themes.label: Pride & Visibility
themes.blurb: Where the need to be admired covers for the fear of being ordinary, or wrong.

prompts.prompt: How do I react when I'm not the center of attention, and what does that reaction protect?
prompts.followUp: What would it feel like to do something well and tell absolutely no one?

prompts.prompt: What is something I find almost impossible to admit I was wrong about?
prompts.followUp: What do I imagine people would think of me if I admitted that mistake out loud?

prompts.prompt: Where in my life am I performing confidence instead of actually feeling it?
prompts.followUp: Who in my life has earned the right to see me uncertain, and when did I last let them?

integrationPrompts: Where do I feel this in my body right now — tight chest, clenched jaw, heavy stomach? Just notice, no need to fix it.
If I spoke to this part of myself with the same compassion I'd offer a close friend, what would I say?
What is one small, low-stakes way I could respond differently the next time this exact pattern shows up?
What would it cost me to keep carrying this — and what might it free up if I set it down, even partially?
Whose voice does the harshest part of this story sound like — and is it actually mine?
What's one tiny act of self-trust I can offer myself today, in spite of all of this?
